title: Grow Records & Diagnostic Worksheets
subtitle: Record what happened before deciding why it happened.
evidenceBoundary: A record improves diagnosis only when observations are separated from interpretations. Preserve units, sample location, time, plant stage, recent changes and uncertainty. A completed worksheet does not by itself confirm a pest, pathogen, nutrient deficiency or environmental disorder.

templates.title: Diagnostic Intake Record
templates.purpose: Capture the minimum whole-case context before assigning a cause.

fields.label: Plant or batch ID
fields.help: Use a stable identifier that connects photos, samples and follow-up notes.

fields.label: Cultivar / source / lot
fields.help: Record the supplied identity and source without treating the name as proof of genetics.

fields.label: Plant stage
fields.help: Seedling, vegetative, transition, flowering, maturation, drying or other defined stage.

fields.label: First symptom date
fields.help: Record when the change was first noticed, not when a diagnosis was guessed.

fields.label: Primary affected organ
fields.help: Leaf, root, stem, meristem, flower, seedling collar or postharvest material.

fields.label: One-sentence neutral description
fields.help: Describe color, shape, distribution and progression without naming the cause.

fields.label: Urgency / crop impact
fields.help: Note whether the issue is localized, spreading, severe, reproductive, or a possible safety/quality concern.

templates.verificationPrompt: Can another grower understand what changed without seeing your proposed diagnosis?

templates.title: Symptom Distribution Map
templates.purpose: Describe where symptoms occur so location becomes diagnostic evidence.

fields.label: Old vs new growth
fields.help: Mark whether symptoms begin on older, middle, newest or all growth.

fields.label: Canopy position
fields.help: Top, middle, lower, edge, interior, shaded or directly illuminated zone.

fields.label: Plant distribution
fields.help: Single plant, cultivar group, irrigation zone, room edge, entire crop or random plants.

fields.label: Tissue pattern
fields.help: Uniform, interveinal, marginal, tip-first, spots, lesions, stippling, distortion or wilting.

fields.label: Progression direction
fields.help: Stable, spreading upward/downward, expanding from a point, or appearing on new sites.

fields.label: Photo set IDs
fields.help: Record whole-plant, affected-tissue and comparison-plant photo identifiers.

fields.label: Unaffected comparison
fields.help: Identify a nearby healthy comparison plant or tissue and how it differs.

templates.verificationPrompt: Does the mapped pattern support more than one plausible cause? Keep those alternatives open.

templates.title: Environment Snapshot
templates.purpose: Record the environment where the affected tissue actually exists, not only a room average.

fields.label: Air temperature + sensor location
fields.help: Include units, canopy height and distance from the affected zone.

fields.label: Relative humidity + sensor location
fields.help: Record units/location and whether the value is instantaneous, minimum, maximum or average.

fields.label: Leaf or surface temperature
fields.help: If measured, record method and location; do not substitute air temperature silently.

fields.label: Light measurement
fields.help: Record PPFD or other light metric, units, instrument and canopy position when relevant.

fields.label: Air movement / exposure
fields.help: Note still zones, direct fan exposure, outdoor wind or obvious airflow differences.

fields.label: Recent environment event
fields.help: Heat spike, cold period, humidity excursion, power outage, rain, wind or equipment change.

fields.label: Comparison-zone readings
fields.help: Record the same measurements in an unaffected or reference zone when possible.

templates.verificationPrompt: Are the measurements from the plant zone that shows the problem, with units and locations preserved?

templates.title: Irrigation & Root-Zone Record
templates.purpose: Separate water-balance, aeration, salinity and root-condition evidence from leaf appearance.

fields.label: Last irrigation time / volume
fields.help: Record when and how much water or solution was applied.

fields.label: Pre-irrigation substrate condition
fields.help: Container mass, moisture sensor, visual/tactile state or other repeatable method.

fields.label: Drainage / runoff behavior
fields.help: Record whether drainage changed, pooled, slowed or differed among containers.

fields.label: pH sample + method
fields.help: Record the actual sample type, collection method, value and meter status.

fields.label: EC sample + method
fields.help: Record units and whether it is source, feed, drain, runoff, extract or another defined sample.

fields.label: Root appearance
fields.help: Color, texture, odor, distribution and whether findings are representative or from one root.

fields.label: Root-zone temperature / oxygen context
fields.help: Record temperature and saturation/oxygenation clues where relevant.

templates.verificationPrompt: Could another person reproduce your pH, EC and moisture measurements from the method notes?

templates.title: Nutrition & Input History
templates.purpose: Document what actually entered the system before calling a symptom a deficiency or toxicity.

fields.label: Base nutrient / recipe ID
fields.help: Use the exact batch or recipe identifier rather than a remembered product name alone.

fields.label: Mix date and operator
fields.help: Connect the symptom window to a traceable preparation event.

fields.label: Measured feed EC / concentration
fields.help: Record units and measurement method.

fields.label: Measured feed pH
fields.help: Record value after mixing and note calibration/check status.

fields.label: Water source / analysis changes
fields.help: Municipal, well, RO, blend or other source; note any recent source change.

fields.label: Additives / foliar / amendments
fields.help: Record all recent additions, including sprays and substrate amendments.

fields.label: Known mixing error or omission
fields.help: Document verified mistakes separately from suspected nutrient explanations.

templates.verificationPrompt: Is there a documented input change that separates one nutrient hypothesis from its look-alikes?

templates.title: Pest & Disease Scouting Record
templates.purpose: Pair symptom patterns with direct organism, lesion and crop-distribution evidence.

fields.label: Scouting route / zone
fields.help: Use a repeatable route or mapped crop zone so counts can be compared over time.

fields.label: Plants / leaves / traps inspected
fields.help: Record the sampling unit instead of a bare pest count.

fields.label: Direct organisms or structures
fields.help: Live pests, eggs, cast skins, webbing, spores, colonies, decay or other direct evidence.

fields.label: Magnification / identification method
fields.help: Record hand lens, microscope, lab test or other method when identification depends on it.

fields.label: Lesion / feeding pattern
fields.help: Stippling, chewing, honeydew, powdery colony, internal rot, root decay or other defined sign.

fields.label: Beneficial organisms / controls present
fields.help: Record predators, parasitoids, biologicals or other controls that affect interpretation of counts.

fields.label: Trend since last scout
fields.help: Increasing, stable, decreasing, newly detected or unresolved; include comparable counts where possible.

templates.verificationPrompt: Do you have direct evidence of an organism or disease process, or only a plant response that could have other causes?

templates.title: Propagation & Plant Identity Record
templates.purpose: Preserve lineage and propagation context when establishment or systemic problems are possible.

fields.label: Mother / seed lot / source ID
fields.help: Keep the upstream source connected to every downstream plant or clone batch.

fields.label: Propagation batch date
fields.help: Record cutting, sowing, transplant or receipt date as applicable.

fields.label: Cutting / seed treatment
fields.help: Record preparation, rooting treatment or germination method without assuming it caused the outcome.

fields.label: Rooting / germination outcome
fields.help: Use defined counts, time-to-event or root-quality observations.

fields.label: Shared tools / water / work area
fields.help: Note connections that could distribute pests, pathogens or process errors.

fields.label: Prior test results
fields.help: Record HLVd or other lab results with date, sample identity and laboratory/method where available.

fields.label: Related plants showing same pattern
fields.help: Map whether siblings, clones or a source plant share the issue.

templates.verificationPrompt: Can you trace this plant backward to its source and forward to every connected clone or batch?

templates.title: Recent Change Timeline
templates.purpose: Find cause candidates by aligning symptom onset with documented system changes.

fields.label: Lighting changes
fields.help: Intensity, fixture height, photoperiod, spectrum or equipment replacement.

fields.label: Irrigation changes
fields.help: Frequency, volume, emitter, drainage, dryback strategy or water source.

fields.label: Nutrition changes
fields.help: Recipe, concentration, pH management, amendment or supplement changes.

fields.label: Environment changes
fields.help: Temperature/RH control, fan position, ventilation, weather or enclosure changes.

fields.label: Plant handling changes
fields.help: Transplant, pruning, training, spraying, cleaning, moving or mechanical injury.

fields.label: New plant / genetics introduction
fields.help: Record incoming material, quarantine status and integration date.

fields.label: Symptom timing relative to changes
fields.help: Write which changes occurred before, during or after symptom onset.

templates.verificationPrompt: Which recent change has a biologically plausible timing and distribution, and what evidence would disprove it?

templates.title: Intervention & One-Change Log
templates.purpose: Make corrective actions testable instead of stacking several changes and losing causal information.

fields.label: Working interpretation
fields.help: State the current best-supported explanation and confidence level.

fields.label: Competing explanation kept open
fields.help: Record at least one plausible alternative that could explain the same symptom.

fields.label: Chosen intervention
fields.help: Describe the smallest justified change or containment action.

fields.label: Why this action was chosen
fields.help: Connect the action directly to evidence, not just a product recommendation.

fields.label: Date / time / crop zone
fields.help: Make the action traceable to the affected plants and observation interval.

fields.label: Variables intentionally held constant
fields.help: List important factors left unchanged so follow-up evidence remains interpretable.

fields.label: Expected observable response
fields.help: Define what should change if the working interpretation is useful.

templates.verificationPrompt: If the plant improves, will the record tell you which change likely mattered?

templates.title: Follow-Up Verification & Case Closeout
templates.purpose: Decide whether the interpretation survived follow-up evidence and preserve what was learned.

fields.label: Follow-up date / interval
fields.help: Record when the crop was rechecked relative to the intervention.

fields.label: New growth / new tissue response
fields.help: Prioritize newly produced tissue when old damage cannot reverse.

fields.label: Symptom incidence / progression
fields.help: New cases, stable area, reduced spread, continued spread or resolved pattern.

fields.label: Repeat measurements
fields.help: Record the same pH, EC, moisture, environment, pest-count or other method used initially.

fields.label: Interpretation status
fields.help: Supported, weakened, rejected, unresolved or replaced by a better explanation.

fields.label: Escalation / testing needed
fields.help: Microscopy, laboratory test, tissue/water analysis, professional diagnosis or additional controlled observation.

fields.label: Case lesson / prevention change
fields.help: Write the process change, baseline or monitoring improvement that should carry into the next crop.

templates.verificationPrompt: Did the follow-up test the original interpretation, or only document that time passed?
